newsitem.title: UK: Kazakhstan given BB minus rating by S&P.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan given BB minus rating by S&P.

text.p: The central Asian republic of Kazakhstan received a BB minus sovereign foreign currency rating from Standard & Poor's on Tuesday, matching the high speculative grade assessment given to Russia a month ago.

S&P said Kazakhstan had made a smooth shift to a market-based economy and had a low debt burden, but the rating was constrained by the country's untested political system, and short track record of orthodox economic and debt management.
The rating falls just below the "investment grade" threshold. There had been speculation in the markets that the oil-rich country would receive a higher rating than Russia.

"The country's relatively successful shift to a marked-based economy...combined with a sharp tightening of fiscal and monetary policies has led to a stabilisation of output this year and a steep reduction in inflation," S&P said.
On the downside, S&P also noted continued weakness in the government's revenue performance, with the brunt of fiscal consolidation still borne by an unsustainable compression of spending.
It saw a risk of slippages in enterprise and banking sector reforms, which could undermine investor confidence and jeopardize monetary and fiscal control.
Kazakhstan is expected to issue a $100 million three-year bond -- its debut Eurobond -- in November.
